newsitem.title: UK: Governor helps save boy in Guam air crash.
newsitem.headline: Governor helps save boy in Guam air crash.

text.p: Guam Governor Carl Gutierrez on Tuesday told how he helped to save an 11-year-old boy from a Korean Air Lines jumbo jet that crashed on the Pacific island with 254 people on board.
"Right now we believe we have found all the survivors and pulled them out. They are now at two hospitals," he told Sky News television in a telephone interview.
Airline officials said earlier as many as 30 people might have survived the disaster.
"We have got hundreds of people combing the hillside and under the debris. I found an 11-year-old boy after the fire. He was burned but he was still conscious.
"There are possibilities that there could be some people still buried under the rubble here that may be survivors."
He said the conditions for rescue workers were very difficult and muddy. "You slip at every step you take and the choppers can't land except maybe about 200 yards away."
The governor said bulldozers were being brought in to carve a road out so that more emergency vehicles could be brought in.
"The tail section (of the aircraft) is still intact. The engines are laying around it. The mid section is completely burned out. The front end broke off on the other side of the hill."
Gutierrez said he had spoken with some survivors, including one man who described the airliner's approach to Guam as "uneventful" until the crash itself.
"They thought they were ready to land and touch down when all of a sudden it wasn't the runway, it was like two or three miles short of the runway," the governor said.
